title: oscore observe notifications have no effective replay window: PIV check reads response_window but commit writes replay_window
description: Found by 3x codereview of the rust-oscore observe port (9liz unblock work; two reviewers converged independently, one with an empirical scratch test). In /home/mark/crates/oscore/src/lib.rs (machine-local clone, captured in patches/rust-oscore-local.patch): begin_unprotect_response_inner checks the response/notification PIV with is_response_reuse (~lib.rs:1308), which reads response_seq/response_window — but that window is only ever written by mark_response_used from the SERVER-side no-PIV branch of protect_response (~lib.rs:1111). PendingResponse::commit writes the PIV into the inbound REQUEST replay window via update_replay_window (lib.rs:259-261). Check window != commit window, so on a client the checked window is never initialized and is_response_reuse is always false: a captured notification (or explicit-PIV response) replays indefinitely at the OSCORE layer (AEAD intact). The doc comment on begin_unprotect_observe_response claims 'freshness is enforced by the response Partial IV replay window' — that enforcement does not exist. Ordinary responses are masked by the request-PIV one-shot guard; observe deliberately skips it (by design), leaving notifications as the one unprotected class. In-tree impact contained: lichen-node commits unconditionally but lichen-coap ObserveClient::process rejects Duplicate/Stale via the authenticated Class-E Observe sequence (lichen-coap/src/observe.rs:678-697). Fix direction: check the notification/response PIV with is_replay (the recipient window commit already writes — self-consistent, since response PIVs and request PIVs share the peer sender-seq space per RFC 8613; mirrors the pre-port unprotect.rs:199 design), or commit into response_window via mark_response_used. Must fix in the local clone + regenerate patches/rust-oscore-local.patch + add a notification-replay test; upstream push of the crate needs Mark's authorization.
